capability: Contain every managed Windows child launch to one explicit inherited-handle allowlist
searchEvidence: ManagedProcessLifetimeLease, Application READY, Launcher READY, Bootstrap START, and Bootstrap ADMITTED currently become ambient inheritable handles before ordinary Process.Start.
AnonymousPipeManagedApplicationProcess, AnonymousPipeManagedLauncherProcess, and StableLauncherHandoff are the existing managed process-launch producers; Application remains the policy owner.

SystemExternalProcessRunner and WindowsExplorerFileRevealService are the only other production Process.Start callers and must share the same process-local launch gate without adopting managed protocol semantics.
LauncherBootstrapRuntime captures outer READY as a raw string and InheritedPipeApplicationReadySignal delays capture, so descendant inheritance is not currently prevented at process entry.

The frozen candidate ledger is 130,153 full production, 92,495 runtime, 20,632 Domain plus Profiles, 40,425 Application, 4,347 host, and 27,091 Infrastructure/Contracts/worker/Platform nonblank lines; the four runtime slices sum exactly to 92,495.
semanticOwner: Platform Windows child-process creation; Version Management Infrastructure typed inherited-handle transport binding
terminalContract: One low-level Platform owner serializes every production Process.Start in this process. Managed Windows launches use CreateProcessW with STARTUPINFOEX and PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST over short-lived inheritable duplicates only: Bootstrap receives START, ADMITTED, and Bootstrap lifetime; Launcher receives Launcher READY and Launcher lifetime; Desktop receives Application READY and Application lifetime; direct legacy Bootstrap receives an empty set. Original authority handles remain non-inheritable. Unknown ambient handles, marker/root/custody handles, and handles from a concurrent launch are not inherited. Final executable custody validation runs inside the same serialized start scope immediately before native creation. Child entry captures typed pipe handles and clears inheritance before any descendant launch. Duplicate, attribute-list, environment, validation, or CreateProcess failure closes all temporary authority; a post-create failure terminates the suspended child and confirms exit before duplicates are released, surfacing any unconfirmed cleanup. Existing READY/START/ADMITTED/lifetime/Job ordering, state schemas, firmware behavior, and executable-topology residual boundaries do not change.

designReview.evidence: Independent architecture review found the durable negative invariant missing from ADR 0056 and ADR 0062 and approved one Platform native owner using STARTUPINFOEX plus PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, exact per-edge allowlists, process-local start serialization, immediate child-side capture, and a new amending ADR. Application policy, protocol wire shapes, Job/lifetime state machines, executable custody, recovery mutation, and firmware semantics remain unchanged.
